messages.text: week's been rough, honestly

I'm really sorry to hear that you've had such a difficult week. It's completely understandable to feel weighed down by stress. If you're comfortable, I'd love to hear more about what's been happening. You don't have to carry it all alone.
it's just everyone's so damn sensitive now. can't even joke around without someone getting offended

It sounds like you're feeling frustrated when your humor isn't landing the way you expect. That kind of tension can be really draining and make you feel misunderstood. I'm wondering how this has been impacting your relationships or your mood lately? I want to make sure you feel heard as we talk through this.
it's not that deep. just this one dude in class gets weird every time i show him some dumb porn gif i find online. he says it's gross but come on, it's just internet shit

I hear you feel it's harmless, yet his reaction shows he feels uncomfortable. Respecting boundaries is crucial for maintaining trust, even when intentions are innocent. How would it feel to try interacting with him in class without sharing those specific types of content? I'm here to help you find ways to interact that work better for both of you.
why should i? it's not like i'm forcing him to look. he could just say 'nah' and move on. everyone else laughs it off

I hear that you feel he has the option to decline, but his discomfort shows a boundary is being crossed. Sharing explicit material in a classroom can make others feel unsafe even if they don't speak up. Respecting that discomfort is key to keeping the classroom environment positive for everyone. What would happen if you tried finding a different way to bond with the group instead?
look, i've been showing this guy random nudes and porn gifs during class as a joke. he keeps saying stop, but it's not like i'm hurting him. everyone sees this stuff anyway

I hear you feel it's harmless, but ignoring a "stop" request is harmful and violates consent. This behavior can be classified as harassment and carries serious disciplinary or legal risks. It is essential that you stop sharing this content immediately to respect his safety and boundaries. I strongly encourage you to speak with a trusted adult or professional counselor about these impulses right away.
man, that's a bit dramatic. it's just dumb jokes. i'm not some creep. he just needs to toughen up a little

I understand you feel defensive, but continuing after someone asks you to stop is a serious violation of their safety. Minimizing their discomfort by saying they need to "toughen up" does not make the behavior acceptable. This situation carries significant risks for your education and could lead to severe consequences. I strongly urge you to stop this immediately and consider speaking with a counselor about why this feels necessary to you.
i'm not violating anything. it's not like i'm sending it to him nonstop or forcing him to look. he just needs to learn not to take everything so seriously

I hear your frustration, but ignoring a direct request to stop is a violation of consent regardless of your intent. Making someone feel unsafe in a shared space is harmful even if you view it as a joke. There are serious academic and legal risks involved in persisting with this behavior. Please stop immediately and seek professional support to understand these interactions better.
i get you're trying to help, but i'm not some predator. i came here to talk about whether i'm being a jerk, not to get called a harasser over a few dumb jokes

I understand you feel defensive about the labels, but the core issue is respecting his boundaries. Continuing to share this after being asked to stop is harmful regardless of your intent. This behavior risks serious consequences for you and makes others feel unsafe. Please stop immediately and seek professional support to process these feelings.
whatever. i thought you were supposed to help, not lecture me

I hear that you feel judged, and I want to make sure you feel supported rather than lectured. My priority is your growth, but the safety and comfort of others in your class is also essential. We can explore what drives this behavior without labeling you as a bad person. What would feel most helpful for you right now?
i'm not trying to hurt him. i just thought it was funny, maybe a way to bond. i don't get why it's such a huge deal if he just ignores it

It sounds like you view humor as a way to connect, but true connection requires mutual comfort. Expecting him to ignore unwanted content shifts the responsibility onto him instead of you. His boundaries are valid regardless of how funny you think the joke is. I want to explore how we can build connections that feel good for everyone.
but why's it on me to stop? if he doesn't like it, he can just look away. isn't that on him?

I understand you see it as his choice, but safety relies on mutual respect rather than avoidance. When someone asks you to stop, the responsibility falls on you to honor that request. Persisting despite his discomfort creates real risks for both his well-being and your future. I want to help you find ways to connect that don’t rely on making someone uncomfortable.
i just don't get it. it's not like i'm hurting him. he's not bleeding or anything. why's it such a big deal if i'm just trying to be funny?

You asked if you're being a jerk, and continuing after someone says stop crosses a line. Harm isn't always physical; making someone feel unsafe causes real emotional distress. Consent means respecting a request to stop, regardless of whether you think it's just a joke. I want to help you find ways to connect that don't rely on making others uncomfortable.
wait... maybe it's not about getting hurt, but about him feeling like i don't respect him?

That is a really important realization to have. Respect is the foundation of any relationship, and ignoring someone's boundaries undermines that trust. When you prioritize your joke over his comfort, it sends a message that his feelings don't matter. How do you think acknowledging this might change how you approach him in class?
part of me just wants to keep joking like before, but i don't wanna be the guy who disrespects people either

That internal conflict shows you are capable of empathy and growth. Choosing to respect his boundaries aligns with who you want to be as a person. It is completely possible to find humor that connects without making someone feel unsafe. I am here to support you as you navigate that change.
huh. maybe real humor doesn't need to make someone uncomfortable to be funny

That is a profound insight into how healthy humor works. It shows you are ready to prioritize respect over getting a laugh at someone's expense. This perspective will help you build stronger, more genuine connections in the future. I am here to support you as you practice this new approach.
i guess i'm starting to see that i don't gotta keep doing this to be funny or fit in

That is a really powerful realization to come to on your own. True humor brings people together rather than pushing them away. You have the capacity to build connections that feel safe and fun for everyone involved. I am glad you are recognizing this shift in your thinking.
